trip.title: Japan Packing List
trip.laundry: Once a week roughly (target: Osaka, Tokyo)
trip.strategy: Carry-on only outbound; check Viv's roller home from Tokyo for purchases

sections.title: Clothing
sections.note: With laundry roughly once a week, you need about 8–10 days of clothing. Tokyo shopping will top you up anyway.

items.name: T-shirts / lightweight tops
items.detail: 4–5 each. Neutral colours layer well.

items.name: Long-sleeve base layer
items.detail: 1–2 each. Evenings in Hakone will be cool.

items.name: Jeans or chinos (smart casual)
items.detail: 1 pair. Worn on travel days; smart enough for Yoshitake.

items.name: Lightweight trousers / casual pants
items.detail: 1–2 pairs. More comfortable for temples and long walk days.

items.name: Nice button-up shirt
items.detail: 1. Yoshitake + tea ceremony. Pack wrinkle-resistant.

items.name: Nice blouse
items.detail: 1. Yoshitake, Kobe beef, tea ceremony. Pack wrinkle-resistant.

items.name: Lightweight knit or cardigan
items.detail: 1. Doubles as a top and a layer. Very efficient packing.

items.name: Casual skirt
items.detail: 1. Day-to-night versatile.

items.name: Casual day dress
items.detail: Great for warm Osaka days and exploring.

items.name: Slightly nicer dress
items.detail: Evening dinners, distinct outfit feel.

items.name: Third dress (wildcard)
items.detail: Can dress up or down depending on the day.

items.name: Lightweight down jacket or vest
items.detail: Viv runs cold — more warmth per gram than fleece. Hakone mornings especially.

items.name: Lightweight down or fleece
items.detail: Hakone mornings, Kurama hike, evening layering.

items.name: Packable rain jacket
items.detail: 1 each (already owned). Japan in April = occasional showers.

items.name: Underwear
items.detail: 8 pairs each.

items.name: Socks
items.detail: 8 pairs each. Mix of ankle/no-show and regular.

items.name: Running shorts + shirt
items.detail: 1 set each. Doubles as sleep / lounge wear.

items.name: Swimsuit
items.detail: Yoshiike ryokan has onsen.

items.name: Lightweight scarf
items.detail: Warmth layering, temple coverage, airplane blanket substitute.

sections.title: Footwear
sections.note: You'll average 20,000+ steps/day. Temples require slip-on/off ease. Viv's ballerina flats double as dressy and comfortable.

items.name: Comfortable walking sneakers
items.detail: Worn on the plane. Primary everyday shoe — every city, every temple.

items.name: Running shoes
items.detail: Also handles hikes (Kurama, Fushimi). Pack in bag.

items.name: Ballerina flats
items.detail: Yoshitake, Kobe beef, nicer dinners. Comfortable enough for general use. Slip-on/off easy for temples.

items.name: Packable sandals / flip flops
items.detail: Ryokan indoor use + warm Osaka days. Lightweight.

sections.title: Camera gear
sections.note: Nikon Z5 + 24-120mm f/4 — stays in Alex's 26L day pack. Never check camera gear.

items.name: Nikon Z5 body
items.detail: Keep in carry-on always.

items.name: NIKKOR Z 24-120mm f/4 S
items.detail: Your only lens — leave it mounted to save time.

items.name: EN-EL15c batteries × 2
items.detail: 20-day trip, heavy shooting days. Two minimum — three is smarter.

items.name: SD cards × 2 (64GB+)
items.detail: Two cards, always. Keep the backup in a different bag.

items.name: USB-C / battery charger
items.detail: MH-25a or dual-slot USB charger.

items.name: Lens cloth + UV filter
items.detail: Protection filter stays on. Microfibre cloth for rain days.

items.name: Lightweight camera strap
items.detail: Peak Design Leash or similar — easier than stock strap for all-day carry.

items.name: Tripod or GorillaPod
items.detail: Optional — useful for dawn shots at Bamboo Grove without asking strangers.

items.name: SD card reader
items.detail: For backing up cards to laptop each evening. Small and critical.

sections.title: Toiletries
sections.note: Japanese convenience stores and drugstores stock most toiletries cheaply. Bring travel-size only; resupply in Japan. Deodorant is the exception — bring full sticks.

items.name: Toothbrush + toothpaste
items.detail: Travel-size paste. Hotels often provide brushes but not always.

items.name: Shampoo + conditioner
items.detail: Travel-size or solid bars. Ryokans usually provide; hotels vary.

items.name: Body wash / soap bar
items.detail: Solid bar is TSA-free and lasts longer than liquid.

items.name: SPF 50 sunscreen
items.detail: You'll be outside all day. Buy more in Japan — their sunscreens are excellent.

items.name: Deodorant (full stick)
items.detail: Harder to find in Japan. Bring a full stick each — don't rely on finding it there.

items.name: Razor
items.detail: Disposable or travel-size. Refills available at Japanese drugstores.

items.name: Lip balm (SPF)
items.detail: Lots of outdoor walking and cool mountain days (Hakone, Kurama).

items.name: Hand cream / moisturiser
items.detail: April can be dry. Excellent options to buy in Japan.

items.name: Basic first-aid / meds
items.detail: Ibuprofen, antihistamines, blister plasters, stomach meds, personal prescriptions.

items.name: Skincare routine items
items.detail: Decant into travel sizes. Japanese skincare is world-class if you want to supplement.

items.name: Hair ties / clips
items.detail: Especially for high-humidity days and hikes.

items.name: Makeup essentials (minimal)
items.detail: Keep light. Tokyo has incredible makeup options to explore.

sections.title: Tech & electronics
sections.note: Japan uses Type A plugs — no adapter needed from Canada. Voltage is 100V; most modern devices handle 100–240V automatically.

items.name: Phone
items.detail: Suica, maps, translation, everything lives here.

items.name: eSIM
items.detail: IIJmio, Ubigi, or Airalo. Buy before departure.

items.name: Laptop or iPad
items.detail: For photo backup, itinerary review. One between you is enough.

items.name: USB-C GaN charger (65W+)
items.detail: One multi-port GaN replaces 3 chargers. Charges laptop, phone, camera.

items.name: Power bank (10,000–20,000 mAh)
items.detail: Big walking days drain phones fast. Check airline carry-on limits (≤100Wh).

items.name: USB-C cable × 2
items.detail: One short (for charger), one long (for bedside).

items.name: Earbuds / headphones
items.detail: Long flights, Shinkansen rides. ANC recommended for YYZ–NRT.

items.name: Luggage scale (small)
items.detail: You're checking bags home from Tokyo — avoid surprises at HND.

sections.title: Documents & money
sections.note: Japan is still heavily cash-based. Withdraw yen from 7-Eleven or Japan Post ATMs. Always have ¥5,000–10,000 on hand.

items.name: Passport
items.detail: Valid 6+ months past Apr 30, 2026. Keep digital scans in cloud storage.

items.name: Travel insurance documents
items.detail: Digital + one paper copy. Know the claims phone number.

items.name: Shinkansen vouchers (Klook)
items.detail: Kanazawa→Kyoto and Osaka→Hiroshima. Screenshot + Klook app ready to redeem at green machines.

items.name: Suica card (Apple/Google Wallet)
items.detail: One each — cannot be shared. Load before Tokyo arrival.

items.name: Credit card (no FX fees)
items.detail: Visa or Mastercard preferred. Amex has limited acceptance in Japan.

items.name: Cash (yen) — withdraw on arrival
items.detail: Get ¥30,000–50,000 from 7-Eleven ATM at NRT. Avoid airport exchange rates.

items.name: Tea ceremony booking confirmation
items.detail: Apr 17, 15:30 — Hanamikoji Street. Screenshot offline.

items.name: Sushi Yoshitake confirmation
items.detail: Apr 27 — $1,156 paid. Screenshot. Arrive exactly on time.

items.name: Kobe beef reservation (Apr 19)
items.detail: Ishida Osaka — screenshot + note address.

sections.title: Daily carry
sections.note: What lives in Alex's 26L and Viv's 30L weekender every day while sightseeing.

items.name: Reusable water bottle
items.detail: Tap water is safe everywhere in Japan.

items.name: Compact folding umbrella
items.detail: For days when the packable jacket feels overkill.

items.name: Hand sanitiser + tissues
items.detail: Many public restrooms have no paper towels or soap. Essential.

items.name: Blister plasters (a few in bag)
items.detail: Even great shoes betray you on 25,000-step days. Compeed are worth it.

items.name: Snacks
items.detail: Konbini tops you up daily, but a couple of energy bars for early morning hikes is smart.

items.name: Packable tote bag
items.detail: Japan is a shopping gauntlet. Always have a bag for impulse buys.

tips.title: Laundry strategy
tips.detail: Coin laundries are everywhere. Wash+dry cycle costs ¥600–1,000, takes ~90 min. Target Osaka (4 nights) and Tokyo (4 nights) as your laundry days.

tips.title: Tokyo shopping buffer
tips.detail: Leave meaningful space in Viv's 40L roller — it becomes the checked bag home. Alex might want a packable duffel inside the 40L for overflow.

tips.title: Temple etiquette footwear
tips.detail: Many temples require removing shoes quickly. Slip-on shoes save time at Kiyomizudera, ryokans, and the tea ceremony.

tips.title: Buy in Japan
tips.detail: Sunscreen, skincare, snacks, and convenience items are cheaper and often higher quality in Japan. A drugstore run on Day 1–2 can stock you up.

tips.title: Hakone will be cooler
tips.detail: Apr 24–26 in Hakone averages 8–15°C. Fleece/down and rain jacket earn their keep here. The ryokan provides yukatas and slippers for indoor use.

tips.title: For Sushi Yoshitake (Apr 27)
tips.detail: Smart casual is fine for a 3-Michelin-star omakase. Nice jeans + button-up is perfect. Avoid strong perfume/cologne — it interferes with the food experience.

tips.title: Back up photos daily
tips.detail: Import cards to laptop each evening. 20 days on one SD card is a single point of failure. Cloud backup over hotel Wi-Fi if bandwidth allows.

tips.title: Urgent: Hiroshima → Odawara
tips.detail: Shinkansen via SmartEx still flagged as unbooked. Golden Week proximity makes this time-sensitive — book as soon as possible.
